title: AI and the research assistant: Evidence from economics working papers
abstract: arXiv:2608.08437v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Studies of AI in science observe isolated tasks or the authors on a byline. They do not observe the research assistants whose data cleaning, coding, literature search, and replication work language models now perform. Economics working papers record this junior labour in their acknowledgements, next to the full text. Using 24 working-paper series through October 2026, I compare papers by the same economist that do and do not disclose AI use, alongside a detector of AI-like prose. Disclosing papers credit 0.548 more named assistants than other papers by the same economist, two-thirds of the mean, and run longer, mostly in their appendices. Disclosures of operational use, such as coding and data work, carry the whole assistant difference; writing-only disclosures and AI-like prose show no consistent association with assistants or pages. translated_title: AI与研究助理：来自经济学工作论文的证据
translated_abstract: 关于AI在科学中应用的研究往往只观察孤立的任务或署名作者，却未能观察到那些如今由语言模型承担数据清洗、编程、文献检索与复现工作的研究助理。经济学工作论文在致谢部分、紧邻正文之处记录了这类初级劳动者的贡献。本文利用截至2026年10月的24个工作论文系列，比较了同一经济学家披露与未披露AI使用的论文，并结合一个检测AI风格文本的工具。与同一经济学家的其他论文相比，披露AI使用的论文多致谢0.548名具名助理（约占均值的2/3），且篇幅更长，主要增加在附录部分。编程、数据处理等操作性使用的披露承载了全部的助理差异；仅与写作相关的披露以及AI风格文本与助理数量或页数之间没有一致的关联。本文将致谢中的初级劳动与选择性的团队披露纳入科学产出的研究之中。
tldr: 本文首次利用经济学工作论文的致谢信息，发现披露AI使用的论文会致谢更多研究助理（初级劳动力），且这一效应完全来自编程与数据处理等操作性AI使用，而非写作用途。
en_tdlr: Exploiting acknowledgements in economics working papers, this paper shows that AI-disclosing papers credit significantly more research assistants, an effect driven entirely by operational AI use (coding and data work) rather than writing-related use.
